subject: Physics
description: Nuclear physics — fission, fusion, chain reactions, atomic bombs, hydrogen bombs, nuclear reactors, India's nuclear programme.

options.option_text: Splitting heavy nucleus into lighter ones
Capturing a free electron in atom

questions.explanation: NUCLEAR FISSION — SPLITTING of a HEAVY NUCLEUS (e.g., URANIUM-235, PLUTONIUM-239) into TWO LIGHTER NUCLEI (fission products) + 2-3 NEUTRONS + ENORMOUS ENERGY (~200 MeV per fission). DISCOVERY: by OTTO HAHN + FRITZ STRASSMANN (1938, Germany) + LISE MEITNER (theoretical, 1939). NOBEL: Hahn 1944. KEY SAMPLE REACTION: U-235 + n → Ba-141 + Kr-92 + 3n + ENERGY (~200 MeV). CHAIN REACTION: each fission releases 2-3 neutrons → trigger more fissions → exponential growth. CRITICAL MASS: minimum mass needed to sustain chain reaction (e.g., U-235 ~50 kg as sphere; reduced to ~15 kg with reflectors). APPLICATIONS: (1) NUCLEAR REACTORS — controlled fission (slow neutrons + control rods). (2) NUCLEAR WEAPONS — uncontrolled fission (atomic bomb). NUCLEAR FUSION — JOINING of light nuclei (e.g., H + H → He). Powers SUN + STARS; theoretically limitless clean energy if commercialized. CONTRAST: FISSION (split) vs FUSION (join). FUSION releases MORE energy/kg than fission. INDIA's NUCLEAR PROGRAMME: started 1948 under HOMI BHABHA ('father of Indian nuclear programme'). KEY MILESTONES: (1) 1956 — APSARA (1st reactor in Asia, BARC, Mumbai). (2) 1969 — TARAPUR (1st commercial nuclear power plant, with USA). (3) 1974 — POKHRAN-I 'Smiling Buddha' nuclear test. (4) 1998 — POKHRAN-II 5 tests. (5) 2008 — INDIA-USA NUCLEAR DEAL. UPSC angle: nuclear policy + Atomic Energy Commission. PYQ FREQUENCY: fission basics in NEET, JEE-Main 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which of these powers the SUN and stars?
questions.explanation: THE SUN — powered by NUCLEAR FUSION in its CORE: HYDROGEN nuclei FUSE into HELIUM, releasing energy. PROCESS: PROTON-PROTON CHAIN (~99% of energy in SUN-like stars): (1) 2H + 2H → He-3 + γ. (2) Multiple steps eventually produce He-4. NET: 4H → He + 2 positrons + 2 neutrinos + 26.7 MeV ENERGY. LARGER STARS use CNO CYCLE (Carbon-Nitrogen-Oxygen catalytic cycle). SOLAR ENERGY: SUN converts ~620 million tonnes of H/sec into ~616 million tonnes of He; ~4 million tonnes of MASS converted to ENERGY (E=mc²) per second! Sun's lifetime fueling: ~5 billion more years. EARTH receives ~1.4 kW/m² of solar power (insolation). FUSION on EARTH (research): (1) TOKAMAK — magnetic confinement; e.g., ITER (France, multinational, target 2035 for first plasma; commercial fusion ~2050). (2) STELLARATOR — alternative magnetic design (Wendelstein 7-X, Germany). (3) INERTIAL CONFINEMENT — laser-fired fuel pellets (NIF, USA — achieved IGNITION Dec 2022). (4) INDIA: SST-1 (Steady State Tokamak-1, Gandhinagar); ITER member-country contributing. ADVANTAGES of fusion over fission: (a) NO long-lived radioactive waste. (b) FUEL is hydrogen — abundant. (c) NO meltdown risk. (d) Massive energy density. CHALLENGES: extreme temperatures (~150 million K) needed; magnetic confinement; net-energy gain elusive (most experiments INPUT > OUTPUT until 2022 NIF breakthrough). UPSC angle: India's energy security + clean energy. PYQ FREQUENCY: Sun = fusion in NEET, NCERT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: INDIA's first NUCLEAR test was conducted in:
questions.explanation: POKHRAN-I (codenamed 'SMILING BUDDHA' / 'Operation Pokhran' / 'Pokhran-I') — INDIA's FIRST NUCLEAR TEST conducted on 18 MAY 1974 at POKHRAN test range, Rajasthan. PM: INDIRA GANDHI. Lead: HOMI SETHNA (Atomic Energy Commission Chair) + RAJA RAMANNA (Director, BARC). YIELD: ~8 KILOTONS (some estimates 12 kT). DESIGNATED: 'PEACEFUL NUCLEAR EXPLOSION' (PNE) by India — triggered international SANCTIONS but India maintained position. POKHRAN-II (Operation Shakti) — 5 tests conducted 11-13 MAY 1998 under PM ATAL BIHARI VAJPAYEE. 11 May: 3 tests (fission + boosted fission + thermonuclear/H-bomb claim). 13 May: 2 sub-kiloton tests. POKHRAN-II made India a DECLARED NUCLEAR-WEAPON STATE. RESPONSE: Pakistan reciprocated with 6 tests in May-June 1998 ('Chagai-I, II'). USA imposed sanctions; lifted gradually. INDIA-USA NUCLEAR DEAL (123 Agreement) — signed 2008 under Manmohan Singh + George W. Bush; allowed civil nuclear trade. NUCLEAR DOCTRINE of INDIA (declared 2003): (1) NO FIRST USE (NFU) — India will not initiate nuclear strike. (2) MASSIVE retaliation if attacked. (3) Non-use against non-nuclear states. (4) Continue to support GLOBAL DISARMAMENT. INDIA HAS NOT signed NPT (Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, 1968) — considers it discriminatory. PYQ FREQUENCY: Pokhran tests in UPSC, SSC, NDA modern history 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: In a NUCLEAR REACTOR, the role of CONTROL RODS is to:
questions.explanation: NUCLEAR REACTOR COMPONENTS: (1) FUEL — typically enriched URANIUM-235 (~3-5% in commercial reactors) or PLUTONIUM-239. Forms FUEL RODS. (2) MODERATOR — slows neutrons (slow neutrons more efficient at causing U-235 fission). Common moderators: WATER (light), HEAVY WATER (D₂O — used in Indian PHWRs), GRAPHITE. (3) CONTROL RODS — ABSORB NEUTRONS to regulate chain reaction. Materials: BORON, CADMIUM, HAFNIUM, INDIUM. INSERT MORE → fewer free neutrons → reaction slows. WITHDRAW → more neutrons → reaction speeds up. EMERGENCY (SCRAM): all rods quickly inserted to halt reaction. (4) COOLANT — removes heat from core (water, gas, liquid sodium). (5) CONTAINMENT — concrete-steel shell prevents radiation leak. (6) STEAM GENERATOR / TURBINE — heat → steam → spins turbine → electricity. INDIA'S NUCLEAR REACTOR FLEET (as of 2024): 22 operational reactors at 7 sites; ~7,500 MW installed capacity. KEY SITES: TARAPUR (Maharashtra, 4 reactors), KAIGA (Karnataka, 4), KUDANKULAM (Tamil Nadu, 2 — Russia-built; more under construction), KAKRAPAR (Gujarat, 4), RAWATBHATA (Rajasthan, 6), NARORA (UP, 2). MOST INDIAN reactors are PHWRs (Pressurized Heavy Water Reactors, 'CANDU'-derived) — use NATURAL uranium + heavy-water moderator. INDIA's 3-STAGE NUCLEAR PROGRAMME (Bhabha Plan): (1) PHWR + natural uranium. (2) FAST BREEDER REACTORS using Pu-239. (3) THORIUM-based reactors (India has world's largest thorium reserves — Kerala beach sands). UPSC angle: nuclear energy + climate change. PYQ FREQUENCY: reactor components in NEET, JEE-Main, UPSC PT 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which is INDIA's LARGEST NUCLEAR POWER PLANT (by installed capacity)?
questions.explanation: KUDANKULAM NUCLEAR POWER PLANT (KKNPP) — TIRUNELVELI district, TAMIL NADU; INDIA's largest single nuclear plant by capacity. CURRENT: 2 operational VVER-1000 reactors (Russian design); each ~1,000 MW = 2,000 MW total. Under construction: Units 3-6 (each 1,000 MW) — additional 4,000 MW; total planned ~6,000 MW (largest in India when complete). PARTNERSHIP: India + RUSSIA (Rosatom); started 1988 (cooperation MoU); construction Unit 1 began 2002, commissioning 2013. CONTROVERSY: massive PROTESTS by local fishermen + activists (~2011-12) over nuclear-safety concerns; SC dismissed petitions 2013, allowing operation. ALSO IMPORTANT: (1) RAWATBHATA (Rajasthan) — 6 PHWR units, 1,180 MW + Unit 7-8 under construction (1,400 MW). (2) TARAPUR (Maharashtra) — INDIA's OLDEST (commissioned 1969); 4 units total ~1,400 MW. (3) KAIGA (Karnataka) — 4 units, 880 MW. (4) KAKRAPAR (Gujarat) — 4 units, 880 MW. (5) NARORA (UP) — 2 units, 440 MW. INDIA's TOTAL: ~7,500 MW installed; ~3% of total electricity (vs ~10% in some countries; 70% in France). FUTURE TARGETS: 22,480 MW by 2031 (per Nuclear Power Corp). PWR programme: Kudankulam + Jaitapur (Maharashtra, with France) — large reactors. INDIGENOUS PHWR programme: Kakrapar 3-4 (700 MW each) commissioned 2023-24 — India's largest PHWRs. KEY ORGANIZATIONS: NPCIL (Nuclear Power Corp of India Ltd) — operates plants. AERB (Atomic Energy Regulatory Board) — safety. UPSC angle: nuclear power in India's energy mix. PYQ FREQUENCY: Indian nuclear plants in UPSC PT, SSC GA 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: EINSTEIN's MASS-ENERGY equation E = mc² shows that:

options.option_text: Energy can never be destroyed only
Light has very high mass always

questions.explanation: E = mc² (Einstein, 1905, Special Relativity): MASS (m) and ENERGY (E) are EQUIVALENT and INTERCONVERTIBLE; c = speed of light (~3 × 10⁸ m/s). The c² factor is HUGE: 9 × 10¹⁶ m²/s² → 1 kg of mass converts to 9 × 10¹⁶ J ≈ 21.5 MEGATONS of TNT! NUCLEAR REACTIONS: a tiny mass-defect (mass of products < mass of reactants) is converted to enormous energy. KEY EXAMPLES: (1) FISSION: 1 g of U-235 fully fissioned → ~24,000 kWh of energy ≈ ~3 tonnes of coal. (2) FUSION: 1 g of D-T fusion → ~100,000 kWh ≈ 12 tonnes of coal. (3) HIROSHIMA bomb: ~700 mg mass converted, equivalent to ~15 KILOTONS TNT. (4) SUN: converts ~4 million tonnes mass/SECOND (already mentioned). REAL-WORLD VERIFICATION: nuclear reactors + accelerator experiments routinely confirm E=mc². ANNIHILATION: matter + antimatter → pure energy (full E=mc² conversion). 1 g of antimatter would yield 1 g × 2 × c² = ~50 megatons. ANTIMATTER PRODUCTION today: ~10⁻¹² grams/year (rare!). INDIA — BHABHA's HYPOTHESIS (1930s): high-energy cosmic rays carrying particles. EINSTEIN: visited India 1922 (briefly); INDIRA GANDHI's grandfather Motilal Nehru attended. PUBLIC AWARENESS: 'E=mc²' is the most famous equation in science. UPSC angle: science + tech in current affairs; energy-physics fundamentals. PYQ FREQUENCY: E=mc² basics in NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which isotope is mostly used as FUEL in commercial nuclear reactors?
questions.explanation: URANIUM-235 (U-235) — primary fuel for most commercial nuclear reactors. KEY: U-235 is FISSILE (can sustain chain reaction with thermal neutrons); U-238 (more abundant) is NOT fissile but FERTILE (can absorb neutron + decay to PLUTONIUM-239, which IS fissile). NATURAL URANIUM composition: ~99.27% U-238 + ~0.72% U-235 + traces U-234. ENRICHMENT: most reactors need 3-5% U-235 (LWRs); WEAPONS need ~90% (HEU, Highly Enriched). India's PHWRs use NATURAL uranium (no enrichment) thanks to heavy-water moderator. ENRICHMENT METHODS: (1) GASEOUS DIFFUSION (old). (2) GAS CENTRIFUGES (modern; India + Iran + many use this). (3) LASER ENRICHMENT (research). KEY ISOTOPES + ROLES: (1) U-235 — FISSILE (used in reactors + bombs). (2) U-238 — FERTILE (breeder reactor fuel). (3) Pu-239 — FISSILE (weapons-grade; bred from U-238). (4) Th-232 — FERTILE (can breed U-233). (5) U-233 — FISSILE (from Th breeding). INDIA's THORIUM ADVANTAGE: ~25% of world's thorium reserves (Kerala monazite sands; ~5 lakh tonnes). 3-STAGE PROGRAMME aims to use thorium in stage 3. RECENT: KAKRAPAR-3 commissioned 2023 — INDIGENOUS 700 MW PHWR. FUEL RODS: enriched UO₂ pellets stacked in zircaloy tubes; bundle of rods = fuel assembly. SPENT FUEL → cooled in pools → reprocessed (BARC's Tarapur reprocessing). NUCLEAR WASTE: glassified high-level waste; storage at Tarapur, Kalpakkam. UPSC angle: nuclear materials + non-proliferation; India's strategic posture. PYQ FREQUENCY: U-235 in NEET, JEE-Main, NCERT 1× per cycle.
